newsitem.title: PERU: Peru hostage crisis could last months - Fujimori.
newsitem.headline: Peru hostage crisis could last months - Fujimori.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said on Thursday the 44-day-old hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima could last several months.

"It could go on a lot longer still. I am patient for the hostages to be freed safe and sound ... It could take some weeks, some months," Fujimori said in an interview with Argentina's CVN television network.
Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages inside the diplomatic mansion have refused to give up their captives unless the government frees 400 jailed comrades.
Fujimori, who was scheduled to leave later on Thursday for a meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto in Toronto on Saturday, has flatly rejected the rebels' demands.
The meeting in Toronto is aimed at achieving "a very close coordination," he said. "If we were in an emergency situation we would need to be in close contact."
The roughly 15 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels stormed a cocktail party at the residence Dec. 17 and seized hundreds of guests. Most were later released.
